questions.q: How many threads does asyncio use to wait for 100 supplier calls?
options: One: a single event loop juggles all the waiting tasks
questions.explain: The event loop runs one coroutine until it awaits, then switches to another. One thread, many waits.

questions.q: What does await mean inside async def?
options: Pause this coroutine here until the thing is done, and let the event loop run other tasks meanwhile
questions.explain: await is a pause point. That's why all three 'ask' lines print before any 'reply'.

questions.q: asyncio.gather(a, b, c) with waits of 0.3 s, 0.1 s and 0.2 s. About how long in total?
questions.explain: All three wait together, so the total is the longest wait. The results come back in the order you passed them: [300, 100, 200].

questions.q: In the lab, 100 supplier calls of 0.1 s each took about how long one by one, and with asyncio?
options: About 10.6 s one by one, about 0.2 s with asyncio
questions.explain: One by one, the waits add up. With asyncio (or threads), they overlap.

questions.q: An async function calls time.sleep(0.1). Ten of them, gathered, take 1.0 s. Why?
options: time.sleep blocks: it never gives control back to the event loop, so the tasks run one after another
questions.explain: Use await asyncio.sleep(0.1) (and async libraries) inside async code. The fix brought it to 0.1 s.

questions.q: price = fetch_price("Patel Spices") inside async def, without await. What is price?
options: A coroutine object, and Python warns: coroutine 'fetch_price' was never awaited
questions.explain: Calling a coroutine only creates it. await it (or gather it) to run it.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Why use asyncio.Semaphore or a connection limit when calling 1,000 supplier APIs?
options: To make it slower on purpose
So you don't open 1,000 requests at once and overload the suppliers (or yourself)
Because asyncio can only do 10 at a time
questions.explain: A Semaphore lets only N run at once; add timeouts too, so one dead supplier can't hang everything.

questions.q: (Going deeper) You must call an old blocking library from async code. What's the safe way?
options: await asyncio.to_thread(old_function, ...): it runs in a thread, and the loop keeps going
questions.explain: Wrapping a blocking call in async def doesn't make it non-blocking. to_thread moves it off the loop.
